{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''David Webb''' is an American [[mathematician]] known for his work on [[hearing the shape of a drum]].

Webb attended [[Cornell University]], where he received his PhD in 1983 under the supervision of [[Kenneth Brown (mathematician)|Kenneth Stephen Brown]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=79190|name=David Webb}}</ref> He is currently a professor of mathematics at [[Dartmouth College]] in [[Hanover, New Hampshire]].<ref>[http://dartmouth.edu/faculty-directory/david-lea-webb Faculty directory listing] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202163743/http://dartmouth.edu/faculty-directory/david-lea-webb |date=2014-02-02 }}, retrieved 2014-01-18.</ref>

In 2001 Webb and co-author [[Carolyn S. Gordon]] were awarded the [[Mathematical Association of America]] [[Chauvenet Prize]] for their 1996 ''[[American Scientist]]'' paper, "You can't hear the shape of a drum".<ref>[http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/chauvenet-prizes Chauvenet Prizes] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628175100/http://maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/chauvenet-prizes |date=June 28, 2017 }}, [[Mathematical Association of America]], retrieved 2014-01-19.</ref><ref name="Gordon Webb 1996 pp. 46–55">{{cite journal | last=Gordon | first=Carolyn | last2=Webb | first2=David | title=You Can't Hear the Shape of a Drum | journal=American Scientist | publisher=Sigma Xi, The Scientific Research Society | volume=84 | issue=1 | year=1996 | issn=00030996 | jstor=29775597 | pages=46–55 | url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/29775597 | access-date=2022-11-15}}</ref>
